extracted.intended_audience: readers of John Locke; and users/distributors of Project Gutenberg eBooks
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on (A) clear, accessible philosophical writing as given in John Locke's preface and introduction, and (B) the procedural and license requirements for distributing a Project Gutenberg eBook (including display, format, trademark, and fee/royalty rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Determinate / Determined ideas (use precise terms)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer the terms 'determinate' or 'determined' instead of vague 'clear and distinct' — an idea should be an immediate object of the mind, perceived and fixed to a name without variation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Locke explains that using determinate ideas (precisely conceived simple or complex ideas attached steadily to a name) prevents much obscurity and disagreement; writers should ensure terms have a precise determination in their present discourse to avoid confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use plain, familiar, intelligible language
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid uncouth, affected, or unintelligible terms introduced as mysteries of science; philosophy should be made plain and familiar to readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Locke argues that vague and misapplied words have been misused to masquerade ignorance as deep learning, and that making subjects intelligible to as many readers as possible is a primary aim of the author.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adapt treatment to intended audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not write primarily for masters of knowledge; aim to be intelligible to readers of the author's own size — better to be tedious to the speculative than obscure to novices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Locke states the Essay was not meant for those who have already mastered the subject; writers should consider the readers' background and prefer clarity for the less trained, even at the risk of appearing long-winded to experts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examine the understanding's capacities before inquiry
rubrics_metrics.description: Before investigating difficult subjects, examine our own abilities and the objects our understanding is fitted to deal with; know the bounds of opinion and knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Locke recommends checking what objects our minds can properly apprehend to avoid fruitless disputes about things beyond our comprehension and to regulate assent where knowledge is uncertain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method: investigate origin, certainty, extent, and assent
rubrics_metrics.description: A clear method: (1) inquire into the origin of ideas/notions; (2) determine what knowledge the understanding gains from them and its certainty/extent; (3) examine the nature and grounds of faith or opinion and degrees of assent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Locke gives this three-part methodology as a rubric for philosophical inquiry — a writer or investigator should state aims and follow these stages when analyzing human knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accept and explain revisions and additions in new editions
rubrics_metrics.description: When issuing new editions, add clarifications, corrections, and explicit explanations to prevent misreadings; transparently indicate significant alterations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Locke documents added chapters and corrections across editions and counsels authors to note what has been altered (e.g., terminology choices like 'determinate'), so readers understand changes and reasons.

rubrics_metrics.description: When a Project Gutenberg electronic work is accessed, displayed, or distributed, the full Project Gutenberg License must accompany it and the specified prominent sentence (1.E.1) must appear with active links or immediate access to the full license.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraphs 1.E.1 and related sections require that the sentence stating the eBook is for use under the Project Gutenberg License appear prominently whenever the work is made available; this is required for works 'associated' with the phrase 'Project Gutenberg.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not unlink, detach, or remove the full Project Gutenberg License
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not unlink, detach, or remove the full Project Gutenberg License terms from this work or any files containing any part of it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 1.E.4 specifically forbids removing the license terms from files containing the work; distributors must keep the license attached to distributed copies unless they comply with other specific permissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prominently display required sentence and active links when distributing
rubrics_metrics.description: The exact sentence in 1.E.1 (about free use under the Project Gutenberg License and link to www.gutenberg.org) must appear prominently with active links or immediate access whenever any copy of a Project Gutenberg work is accessed, displayed, performed, viewed, copied or distributed.

rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 1.E.6 allows format conversion but requires distributors to make the original official format available upon request at no cost to the user.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules when charging a fee: royalty, refunds, and conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: You may charge a reasonable fee for copies/access only if you: pay a 20% royalty of gross profits to the trademark owner (donated to the Foundation), provide refund policies (full refund to users who disagree within 30 days or on defective copies within 90 days), and comply with all other free-distribution terms.
